findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body: After `attach()` registers the handler, invoking its returned disposer now does nothing. Subsequent messages still invoke the stale handler, while repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and cause duplicate processing. This directly reverses the existing cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
When a caller invokes the returned disposer and the socket later emits `"message"`, the handler remains registered and still runs. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
The returned cleanup function no longer detaches the handler. If a session or authorization boundary calls it during teardown while an untrusted peer can still send socket messages, that peer can continue invoking the stale privileged handler; repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate handlers and permit resource exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
